hobbiton.summary: A quiet hobbit village on the Water, with Bag End dug into the Hill above it. Bilbo and later Frodo lived here, and the whole story of the Ring begins and ends at this doorstep.

storyEvents.text: Gandalf scratches a sign on Bilbo's door and thirteen dwarves arrive for tea, launching the quest to Erebor.
Bilbo vanishes at his 111th birthday party and leaves the Ring, and Bag End, to Frodo.
The returning hobbits find the Shire under Sharkey's rule and rally their neighbours to throw the ruffians out.

old-forest.summary: An ancient, watchful wood on the eastern border of the Shire. Its trees move, its paths shift, and Old Man Willow waits by the Withywindle.

storyEvents.text: Frodo, Sam, Merry and Pippin cut through the forest to avoid the Road and are trapped by Old Man Willow until Tom Bombadil sings them free.

barrow-downs.summary: Rolling grassy hills east of the Old Forest, crowned with the standing stones and burial mounds of forgotten kings. Barrow-wights haunt the tombs.

storyEvents.text: The hobbits are caught in fog and captured by a Barrow-wight. Tom Bombadil rescues them, and the blades taken from the barrow later matter greatly to Merry.

bree.summary: A village of both Men and hobbits at the crossing of the East Road and the Greenway, famous for The Prancing Pony inn.

storyEvents.chapter: At the Sign of the Prancing Pony
storyEvents.text: Frodo slips on the Ring in the common room, and a weathered ranger called Strider offers to guide the hobbits.
On the way home the hobbits find Bree changed and wary after a hard year.

weathertop.summary: The southern peak of the Weather Hills, once the site of the watchtower Amon Sûl that held one of the palantíri. Only a ring of broken stones remains.

storyEvents.text: Strider and the hobbits camp below the summit and are attacked by five Black Riders. Frodo is stabbed by the Witch-king's Morgul-blade.

trollshaws.summary: Hilly woodland between the Hoarwell and the Loudwater where trolls once roamed. Three of them still stand there, turned to stone.

storyEvents.text: Bilbo and the dwarves stumble on three trolls arguing over how to cook them. Gandalf keeps them bickering until sunrise turns them to stone.
The company passes the same stone trolls, and Sam recites a song about them.

rivendell.summary: Imladris, the hidden Elven refuge of Elrond in a deep valley at the feet of the Misty Mountains. A place of healing, counsel and old songs.

storyEvents.text: Thorin's company rests here and Elrond reads the moon-letters on Thrór's map.
Elrond heals Frodo, the Council decides the Ring must be destroyed, and the Fellowship of nine is chosen.

high-pass.summary: The main pass over the Misty Mountains east of Rivendell, plagued by goblins who tunnel beneath it.

storyEvents.text: Sheltering from a storm, the company is snatched by goblins through a crack in the cave. In the tunnels below, Bilbo finds a small golden ring.

annuminas.summary: The first capital of Arnor on the shore of Lake Evendim, long abandoned and in ruins by the time of the War of the Ring.

storyEvents.text: Aragorn, as King Elessar, restores the ancient city of his forefathers.

carrock.summary: A great rock standing in the Anduin with steps cut into it by Beorn, whose hall lies nearby.

storyEvents.text: The eagles set the company down on the Carrock, and Gandalf introduces the dwarves to Beorn two at a time.

moria.summary: Khazad-dûm, the greatest dwarf city of the Misty Mountains, now dark and full of orcs. The West-gate opens only to a password written in ithildin.

storyEvents.text: Gandalf finally speaks 'mellon', the Watcher in the Water attacks, and the Fellowship enters the mines.
The Fellowship finds Balin's tomb, is hunted by orcs and a cave-troll, and Gandalf falls with the Balrog from the bridge.

lorien.summary: Caras Galadhon, the city of trees at the heart of Lothlórien, where Galadriel and Celeborn dwell among the golden mallorns.

storyEvents.text: The grieving Fellowship finds rest. Frodo and Sam look into Galadriel's Mirror, and Frodo offers her the Ring.
The company receives elven cloaks, boats and gifts, including the phial that will light Shelob's lair.

dol-guldur.summary: The Hill of Sorcery in southern Mirkwood, the fortress of the Necromancer, who was Sauron in hiding.

storyEvents.text: Gandalf reveals he left the company to help drive the Necromancer out of his stronghold in the south of the forest.

thranduils-halls.summary: The underground halls of the Elvenking beneath the hills of northern Mirkwood, by the Forest River.

storyEvents.text: The dwarves are imprisoned by the Wood-elves, and invisible Bilbo smuggles them out in empty wine barrels.

esgaroth.summary: Lake-town, a trading town of Men built on piles out in the Long Lake, within sight of the Lonely Mountain.

storyEvents.text: The company floats in by barrel and is feasted by the Master of the town, who hopes for gold from the mountain.
Smaug burns Lake-town. Bard the Bowman, told of a gap in the dragon's armour by a thrush, brings him down with the black arrow.

erebor.summary: The Lonely Mountain, kingdom of Durin's folk under Thrór until the dragon Smaug took it. The goal of Thorin's quest.

storyEvents.text: The last light of Durin's Day reveals the keyhole of the secret door.
Bilbo creeps into the hall and trades riddles with Smaug on his hoard.
The Battle of Five Armies is fought before the gate. Thorin is mortally wounded and makes peace with Bilbo.

iron-hills.summary: Dwarf-held hills east of Erebor, home of Dáin Ironfoot, whose army marches to the Lonely Mountain.

storyEvents.text: Dáin's five hundred dwarves arrive from the Iron Hills just before the goblin army descends.

tharbad.summary: A ruined river-town where the North-South Road once crossed the Greyflood by a great bridge, now fallen.

storyEvents.text: Boromir tells of losing his horse at the perilous crossing of Tharbad on his long ride to Rivendell.

fangorn.summary: The last remnant of the great forests of the Elder Days, home of Treebeard and the Ents.

storyEvents.text: Merry and Pippin escape the orcs into the forest and meet Treebeard, the oldest living thing that walks.
Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli track the hobbits to the forest eaves and meet Gandalf, returned from death.

isengard.summary: A ring of stone around the tower of Orthanc, at the southern end of the Misty Mountains. Saruman's fortress and forge.

storyEvents.text: Gandalf recounts how Saruman revealed his treachery and imprisoned him on the pinnacle of Orthanc.
The Ents tear down the walls and drown the pits, and Merry and Pippin greet the arriving riders from the rubble.
Gandalf breaks Saruman's staff and Wormtongue throws the palantír from the tower.

helms-deep.summary: A fortified gorge in the White Mountains guarded by the Hornburg and the Deeping Wall, Rohan's refuge in times of war.

storyEvents.text: Théoden's riders hold the wall through a night of storm against Saruman's host. At dawn Gandalf arrives with Erkenbrand, and the Huorns swallow the fleeing orcs.

edoras.summary: The capital of Rohan on a green hill at the feet of the White Mountains, crowned by the golden hall of Meduseld.

storyEvents.chapter: The King of the Golden Hall
storyEvents.text: Gandalf frees Théoden from Wormtongue's whispers, and the king takes up his sword again.
The Rohirrim gather at Dunharrow and ride for Gondor; Merry rides hidden with Dernhelm.

amon-hen.summary: The Hill of Sight above the falls of Rauros, with an ancient seat of seeing on its summit. Here the Fellowship breaks.

storyEvents.text: Boromir tries to take the Ring. Frodo puts it on, sees the Eye from the Seat of Seeing, and resolves to go on alone with Sam.
Boromir dies defending Merry and Pippin, and his companions send him over the falls in an elven boat.

dead-marshes.summary: A drowned battlefield north-west of Mordor, where the faces of the dead from the Last Alliance glimmer beneath the pools.

storyEvents.text: Gollum leads Frodo and Sam through the marsh by night, warning them not to follow the candle-lights of the dead.

morannon.summary: The Black Gate, a rampart of iron and stone closing the pass of Cirith Gorgor, the only northern way into Mordor.

storyEvents.text: Frodo, Sam and Gollum see the gate is impassable, and Gollum offers another way: the stairs of Cirith Ungol.
The Captains of the West challenge Sauron at the gate to draw his eye from the Ring-bearer.

barad-dur.summary: The Dark Tower, Sauron's fortress, raised with the power of the Ring and unbreakable while the Ring survives.

storyEvents.text: As the Ring goes into the fire, the towers of Barad-dûr crumble and fall.

mount-doom.summary: Orodruin, the volcano where Sauron forged the One Ring, and the only fire hot enough to unmake it.

storyEvents.text: Sam carries Frodo up the mountain. At the Cracks of Doom Gollum bites off the Ring, and falls with it into the fire.

cirith-ungol.summary: The Pass of the Spider, a high cleft in the Ephel Dúath guarded by an orc tower and by Shelob's lair.

storyEvents.text: Gollum leads the hobbits into Shelob's tunnels. Sam drives the spider off, but Frodo lies stung and is taken by orcs.
Sam braves the tower alone and rescues Frodo after the orcs fall to fighting among themselves.

minas-morgul.summary: Once Minas Ithil, Tower of the Moon; now the dead city of the Ringwraiths, glowing with a sickly light.

storyEvents.text: The hobbits watch the Witch-king lead his army out of the city gate to war, while Frodo fights the pull of the Ring.

osgiliath.summary: The old capital of Gondor, built across the Anduin. Ruined by war and plague, its bridge is a battleground.

storyEvents.text: Boromir tells of the dream that came to him and Faramir after the fight for the bridge of Osgiliath.
Faramir holds the ruins as long as he can before the enemy crosses the river in force.

minas-tirith.summary: The White City of seven walls built against Mount Mindolluin, capital of Gondor and seat of the Stewards.

storyEvents.text: Gandalf and Pippin arrive ahead of the war, and Pippin swears service to Denethor.

storyEvents.chapter: The Battle of the Pelennor Fields
storyEvents.text: The Rohirrim break the siege at dawn. Éowyn and Merry slay the Witch-king, and Aragorn arrives by ship.
Aragorn is crowned King Elessar before the gates, and Faramir and Éowyn are betrothed.

pelargir.summary: Gondor's great river-port on the lower Anduin, where the black ships of Umbar are captured.

storyEvents.text: Aragorn and the Dead of Dunharrow take the corsair fleet at Pelargir and sail it up the Anduin to Minas Tirith.

dol-amroth.summary: A castle-city on the coast of Belfalas, home of Prince Imrahil and his swan-knights.

storyEvents.text: Imrahil rides in with his knights to help defend the White City.

umbar.summary: A great natural harbour far to the south, stronghold of the Corsairs who raid Gondor's coasts.

storyEvents.text: The corsair fleet from Umbar sails to attack Gondor, only to be seized by Aragorn at Pelargir.

grey-havens.summary: Mithlond, the elven harbour on the Gulf of Lune, from which the Elves sail west over the Sea.

storyEvents.text: Frodo, Bilbo, Gandalf, Galadriel and Elrond board the white ship and sail into the West. Sam rides home.

shire.summary: A green, well-ordered land of farms and hobbit-holes, sheltered from the wide world for centuries.

eriador.summary: The wide lands between the Blue Mountains and the Misty Mountains, once the kingdom of Arnor, now mostly empty.

lindon.summary: The last Elven realm west of the mountains, ruled from the Grey Havens by Círdan the Shipwright.

angmar.summary: The cold northern realm of the Witch-king, which destroyed Arnor long ago and was itself destroyed in turn.

hollin.summary: Eregion, the former land of the Elven-smiths who forged the Rings of Power. Holly trees still mark its borders.

dunland.summary: Hill country west of the Misty Mountains, home of the Dunlendings, who fought for Saruman at Helm's Deep.

enedwaith.summary: A sparsely peopled wilderness between the Greyflood and the Isen.

rohan.summary: The Riddermark, grassy plains of the horse-lords, allies of Gondor.

gondor.summary: The southern kingdom of the Dúnedain, long without a king, holding the line against Mordor.

ithilien.summary: The garden of Gondor between the Anduin and the Mountains of Shadow, now a wild borderland patrolled by Faramir's rangers.

mordor.summary: The Black Land, walled by mountains on three sides, where Sauron gathers his armies under the shadow of Mount Doom.

rhovanion.summary: Wilderland: the vast country east of the Misty Mountains, holding Mirkwood, the Anduin vales and the Lonely Mountain.

rhun.summary: The little-known East, from which the Easterlings come to serve Sauron.

harad.summary: The sun-lands of the South, home of the Haradrim and their war-oliphaunts.

forodwaith.summary: The frozen Northern Waste beyond Angmar, where few travel.
